home.subtitle: Pick up where you left off.
home.emptyBody: Create your first workspace and start using dsh.

workspaceCreate.title: Create workspace
workspaceCreate.subtitle: Give your dsh workspace a name. We will take care of the rest.
workspaceCreate.name: Name
workspaceCreate.nameHint: Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. This also becomes its private address.
workspaceCreate.readyBody: Your dsh environment is prepared and waiting for you.

files.title: Files
files.subtitle: Open the file environment for any of your workspaces.
files.emptyBody: Create a workspace to start working with files.
files.boundary: Files remain inside each isolated workspace. Open a workspace to upload, create, move, preview, or delete files in dsh.

activity.title: Activity
activity.subtitle: A quiet record of what happened across your workspaces.
activity.emptyBody: Workspace activity will appear here as you work.

workspaceDetail.notFound: This workspace could not be found.

workspaceOpen.offlineBody: Start it when you are ready to continue.
workspaceOpen.errorBody: We could not prepare this workspace.

workspaceSettings.title: Workspace settings
workspaceSettings.subtitle: Everyday preferences first. Runtime details stay out of the way until you need them.

setup.intro: This platform has no domain yet. Create the administrator account (you will use it to sign in), then enter a parent domain: the console will live on its console subdomain, and each workspace gets a subdomain of its own.
setup.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. You will sign in to the console with it.
setup.domainHint: Point the wildcard record *.<domain> at this machine first — certificates cannot be issued before it resolves.
setup.plaintext: There is no certificate yet, so this submission travels over a plaintext connection. It is used once, during first-time setup.
setup.noToken: This link is incomplete (the token is missing). Open this page with the full link the installer printed.
setup.errToken: That token is wrong, or it has already been used. Reopen the link the installer printed.
setup.errConfigured: The platform already has a domain; changes are not accepted here.
setup.errAccountExists: That email already has an account. Use another one — the existing account's password and role are left untouched.
setup.errAccount: The email or password does not qualify: the email must look like name@example.com and the password must be at least 8 characters.
setup.errDomain: That does not look like a domain: lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes only, and at least two labels (for example example.com).
setup.doneBody: The administrator account {{email}} has been created and the platform is restarting (a few seconds). Then open {{domain}} and sign in with it — on the first visit the certificate may still be issuing (seconds to a minute), so wait and reload if you see a certificate error.
setup.doneClose: This page's entry point has been closed — you can close this tab.
setup.doneDns: Note: {{probe}} does not resolve — the wildcard record has not taken effect yet. The account and domain are saved, but until it resolves **you cannot reach `console.<the domain you entered>` either** (and certificates cannot be issued). To get in meanwhile, add a hosts entry or send the Host header yourself.

invite.subtitle: You have been invited
invite.intro: Set a password and you are in.
invite.name: Name
invite.alreadyAccepted: The account was created, but signing in automatically did not work. Go back to the sign-in page and use the password you just set.

instances.title: Workspaces
instances.subtitle: Your personal dsh spaces, ready when you are.
instances.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 3–32 characters.
instances.versionHint: Which dsh build the workspace runs; the list shows every published version.
instances.versionEmpty: No image version has been published yet — ask an admin.
instances.diskHint: A hard limit: once full, the workspace can no longer write. Ask an admin for more space.
instances.newDescription: Pick a subdomain — that becomes its address.
instances.emptyHint: Create your first workspace to start using dsh.
instances.deleteDescription: The container, the address and all data for “{{slug}}” are deleted for good. Just want it to stop? Use Stop — the workspace and its data stay.
instances.deleteFailed: Could not delete the workspace, please retry
instances.pidsHint: 512 is enough by default; raise it for heavy builds ({{min}}–{{max}}).
instances.quotaFull: At the limit — delete one first

instanceDetail.loadFailed: Workspace not found, or not yours
instanceDetail.upgradeHint: Upgrading snapshots your data first, then swaps the image — the workspace is offline while it runs (longer with more data). If the new version fails to start it rolls back automatically.
instanceDetail.noStable: No other versions to switch to right now.
instanceDetail.rollbackTitle: Roll back to the previous version?
instanceDetail.rollbackDescription: The data for “{{slug}}” is restored to the moment before the upgrade — anything written since is lost. The image goes back to {{image}}.
instanceDetail.usageStopped: The workspace is not running — no live CPU or memory, but disk usage still shows.
instanceDetail.usageEmpty: No samples yet — it samples once a minute.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: How your account is identified across DSH Cloud.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: Devices signed in to your account
sessions.revokeFailed: Could not revoke the session, please retry

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password and signed-in devices
account.passwordDescription: Update your password to protect your workspaces and persistent files.
account.emailHint: Changing your email means verifying the new address by mail, and this platform has no mailer configured — ask an operator.
account.passwordTooShort: New password must be at least {{min}} characters.
account.passwordMismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
account.passwordFailed: Could not change password, please retry
account.noPassword: This account has no password (it may have been created by an admin).

overview.title: Admin console
overview.description: Platform operations, separate from personal workspaces.
overview.manageWorkspaces: Runtime state, resources, logs, and recovery
overview.manageVersions: Published dsh releases and host availability

users.title: Users
users.description: Ban or unban accounts, change how many workspaces someone can create, grant or revoke admin.
users.banDescription: {{email}} will be signed out immediately and can no longer sign in.
users.grantAdminConfirm: Make {{email}} a platform admin? Admins can ban accounts, change quotas, and see every workspace and container log.
users.selfDemoteHint: This is your own account: you will lose admin access immediately and be sent back to the home page.
users.inviteDescription: Generate a link and send it yourself. Single use, expires after {{hours}} hours.
users.inviteCopyHint: Copy it and send it yourself — once you leave this page the link is gone for good.

instances.title: All workspaces
instances.description: Status, disk and container logs for every workspace. Logs are readable for troubleshooting; an workspace’s /data filesystem is not.
instances.logHint: Container logs may contain user content — visible for troubleshooting, but admins still cannot browse an workspace's /data filesystem.
instances.imageHint: Changing the image snapshots the data first, then rebuilds the container — the workspace is offline while it runs (longer with more data). If the new image fails to start it rolls back automatically.
instances.imageRollbackConfirm: Roll back to {{image}}? Data written since the upgrade is lost.
instances.imageLocalEmpty: No other images on the host yet
instances.quotaHint: Changing CPU, memory or process limit rebuilds the container — a few seconds of downtime. Growing disk needs no restart; shrinking does. No data is lost.

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: dsh versions your users can create and upgrade to. Publish one and it appears in the version picker on their workspaces.
versions.warmedHint: Cached on this host — the first workspace on this version won't wait for a download
versions.unpublishDefault: The default version can't be unpublished — set another version as default first
versions.unpublishConfirm: {{ref}} disappears from the user-facing version picker; workspaces already running it are unaffected.
versions.notOnHost: Not cached on this host. Creating this version downloads it automatically, but it only appears in a user’s upgrade list after it is pre-warmed here
versions.emptyBody: Users can't create workspaces right now. Check for updates to read the registry, then publish the version you want.
